400.description: Bad request - validation error or duplicate subscriber

Returns a single subscriber with their latest preferences

patch.description: Updates subscriber fields. All fields are optional.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a subscriber. The record is retained but excluded from all queries.

post.description: Upserts up to 500 subscribers per request. Each row is matched to an existing subscriber by publicId, then externalId, then email (in that order); if none match, a new subscriber is created. Rows are processed independently, so one failing row does not fail the batch.

patch.description: Creates a new preference record with updated values (immutable pattern)

post.summary: Add a tag to a subscriber
post.description: Adds a tag to the subscriber. Adding a tag that's already present is a no-op.

delete.summary: Remove a tag from a subscriber

post.description: Called from the unsubscribe confirmation page linked from emails. Verifies the signed token and turns off email notifications for the subscriber it identifies. No API key required.
Starts a run of the workflow identified by `key` for the matched subscriber, scheduling all of its steps.

404.description: Environment, workflow, or subscriber not found

post.description: Creates a workflow definition: a named, ordered sequence of steps (email or webhook), each with a delay relative to the previous step. Optional `triggers` start it automatically on events from connected integrations, e.g. Stripe's trial_started, and `exitConditions` stop a person's active run on others.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of workflows in the environment
Returns a paginated list of trigger runs across every workflow in the environment, most recent first
Returns a single workflow with its steps

patch.description: Updates workflow fields. If `steps` is provided, it replaces ALL existing steps; likewise for `triggers` and `exitConditions`.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a workflow. Existing in-flight runs are unaffected.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of trigger runs for this workflow, most recent first

post.description: Resolves the audience query and returns how many subscribers currently match, without creating or sending anything. Intended for confirming a broadcast's blast radius before triggering it.

400.description: Workflow is paused or has no steps

post.description: Fans this workflow out to every subscriber matching the audience query. Resolving the audience and scheduling sends happens asynchronously — poll the returned broadcast (via listBroadcasts/getBroadcast) for progress.

400.description: Workflow is paused or has no steps

get.description: Returns a paginated list of broadcasts triggered for this workflow, most recent first
Returns a single broadcast with its resolved audience size and derived step-outcome counts (sent/failed/skipped/pending)

post.description: Holds every send that hasn't gone out yet until the broadcast is resumed. Already-sent emails are unaffected.
Lets a paused broadcast carry on sending. The remaining sends keep their original spacing, pushed back by however long it was paused.
Permanently stops a broadcast: every send that hasn't gone out yet is cancelled. Already-sent emails are unaffected. Cannot be undone.

409.description: Broadcast isn't pending, queued or paused

post.description: Re-runs setup for every matching subscriber who hasn't been set up yet (for example after setup jobs failed), spread over a fresh send window. Subscribers already set up are skipped, so nobody receives the email twice.

Generic bounce-recording endpoint, identified by the run step's publicId - callers are expected to have that publicId available via whatever mechanism they use to learn about the bounce (e.g. a provider's native webhook echoing back metadata set at send time). Authenticated with a shared bearer secret (BOUNCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), not an API key. Enqueues the bounce for async processing and returns immediately.

patch.description: Creates or updates the integration of the given type for this environment (e.g. "smtp"). Body shape depends on the integration type; secret fields (e.g. password) are encrypted at rest and never returned. When updating, omit secret fields to keep the stored ones; config fields are always replaced in full.

404.description: Environment or integration type not found

get.description: Returns the sanitized config for a single integration type (no secrets).

patch.description: Moves this integration to the front of the environment's failover order (tried first on send). The rest keep their relative order as fallbacks.

get.description: Returns every integration configured for this environment, sanitized (no secrets).
Subscriber counts, opt-outs, send outcomes, and bounce breakdown for an environment. `days` scopes the new-subscriber and recently-opted-out counts; send/bounce totals are all-time.

Webhook events received from inbound sources (e.g. Stripe) for this environment, most recent first, with the events they matched and what happened (workflow triggered, no workflow triggered by it, person not found, etc.).

parameters.description: Only events from this source, e.g. "stripe".

payload.description: Arbitrary data merged into {{variable}} interpolation alongside subscriber fields.

key.description: Stable identifier used to trigger this workflow, e.g. "user-signup". Unique within the environment.

type.description: Purely organizational: automation workflows are meant to be triggered individually per-subscriber; broadcast workflows are meant to be fanned out via the broadcast endpoint. Either can technically still be used either way.

delayMs.description: Milliseconds to wait after the previous step (or after trigger, for the first step) before sending this step.

body.description: HTML (or plain text) email body, rendered as a Liquid template (https://liquidjs.com). Supports {{ subscriber.firstName }} etc. interpolation from subscriber fields, subscriber.attributes, and the trigger payload, plus {{unsubscribeUrl}} for this subscriber's unsubscribe link, and {% if %}/{% else %}/{% endif %} conditionals, e.g. {% if subscriber.firstName %}Hey {{ subscriber.firstName }}{% else %}Hey there{% endif %}.

url.description: Destination URL the JSON payload is POSTed to.

Use the `json` filter around interpolated values to keep the result valid JSON.

event.description: One of the source's events (see list_trigger_sources), e.g. "trial_started", or a raw event type such as "checkout.session.completed".

triggers.description: Events from connected integrations that start this workflow for the person they're about. Automation workflows only; the integration must be connected first.

exitConditions.description: Events from connected integrations that stop this workflow for the person they're about: their active runs are cancelled and unsent steps never send. Checked before triggers, so an event in both restarts the workflow. Automation workflows only; the integration must be connected first.
